```{r, include = FALSE}
online <- requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE) &&
  !is.null(tryCatch(curlGetHeaders("https://services1.arcgis.com"), error = function(e) NULL))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6.5, dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 110, eval = online)
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(phwstyle)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

## Boundaries for every level

`phw_boundaries()` downloads boundaries from the ONS Open Geography Portal
or DataMapWales, keeps them only for Wales, and caches them so later calls
work offline. The list of releases is kept up to date in the package.

```{r, eval = TRUE}
phw_boundary_levels()
```

Each result is an `sf` data frame with `code`, `name`, `name_cy` (where the
source has Welsh names) and the geometry. Join your own data on `code`.

```{r}
hb <- phw_boundaries("health_board") |>
  mutate(rate = round(runif(n(), 20, 80), 1))

ggplot(hb) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = rate), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_phw_b(name = "Rate per\n100,000") +
  theme_phw_map() +
  labs(title = "Rate by health board", caption = attr(hb, "attribution"))
```

GP clusters, LSOAs and the other levels work the same way. Use
`detail = "super"` or `"ultra"` for smaller files, or `"full"` for coastline
detail.

```{r}
gp <- phw_boundaries("gp_cluster")
ggplot(gp) +
  geom_sf(fill = phw_colours[["light_teal"]], colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  theme_phw_map() +
  labs(title = paste(nrow(gp), "GP clusters"))
```

## Interactive maps

```{r, eval = online && requireNamespace("leaflet", quietly = TRUE)}
phw_leaflet() |>
  phw_leaflet_polygons(phw_boundaries("health_board", crs = 4326) |> mutate(rate = hb$rate),
                       fill = rate, bins = 4, label = name, legend_title = "Rate")
```

## Keeping boundaries up to date

A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow in the repository checks ONS and
DataMapWales every month and opens a pull request when a new release
appears. After updating phwstyle, refresh your cached copies:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
phw_boundaries("electoral_ward", refresh = TRUE)
phw_boundaries_cache(clear = TRUE)   # or clear everything
```
